work.title: FOUNDER NARRATIVE
work.subtitle: 创始人叙事融资稿
work.scope: Fictional fundraising speech template. Spoken drafts, ventures, people and illustrative models are invented; no real traction, validated impact, technical performance, securities offer, investment terms or committed funding is supplied.

pages.title: Start with a small frustration.
pages.lead: We started with a small frustration: a useful note can lose its meaning when the context around it disappears. Margin is our fictional concept for keeping a reading note beside the question that gave it purpose. We are here to explain that direction and the evidence we would need before asking anyone to believe a larger story.
pages.body: Open with a concrete tension, not an invented customer testimonial. Margin and the founder voice are fictional. No real origin story, launch or customer experience is established by this script.

pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.

pages.title: Make the problem recognisable.
pages.lead: Imagine returning to a note that says useful passage but not why it mattered. The problem we want to explore is not a shortage of tools; it is the gap between saving a reference and recovering its intended use. That situation is our design premise, not measured demand.
pages.body: Pause after the example. A real pitch would need appropriate evidence about the intended reader and context. Do not describe the imagined situation as a study finding or a universal behaviour.

pages.title: Explain the founder’s reason to care.
pages.lead: Our interest is in the moment when a reader moves from collecting material to making a careful point. We want the document to show both the reference and the question attached to it. That is the commitment behind this concept, rather than a claim that our background guarantees a successful business.
pages.body: Use an authentic biography only after replacing the fictional voice with verified context. No credentials, employment history, specialist expertise or founder-market fit is supplied here.

pages.title: Introduce the change in approach.
pages.lead: The proposed shift is simple: keep the note, its source and its intended use together. Instead of presenting another place to collect everything, we would explore a smaller structure that helps a reader explain why one item belongs in the next conversation.
pages.body: This is a product intention, not a demonstration of implemented software. Keep the difference between a proposed workflow and a working capability explicit when adapting the script.

pages.title: Walk through one use situation.
pages.lead: A reader selects a passage, writes the question it raises and records what would need checking before the passage supports a claim. The useful result would be a more inspectable note, not an automatic conclusion. This short walkthrough illustrates the intended experience; it is not a tested user journey.
pages.body: Point to a clearly labelled concept artifact if one exists. The illustrations are editorial references, not product screenshots, user research or evidence that a real person completed the workflow.

pages.title: Say what progress would mean.
pages.lead: At this stage, progress would mean learning whether the proposed structure addresses a specific reader task. We would want to see the question become clearer, the reference remain traceable and the limits stay visible. We are not reporting customers, retention or revenue in this fictional narrative.
pages.body: Do not substitute a polished illustration for traction. If real progress is later added, retain its unit, period, denominator and supporting source beside the claim.

pages.title: Keep the business hypothesis separate.
pages.lead: The business question is whether a defined group would value this support enough to adopt it under sustainable conditions. We have not established a price, willingness to pay or a repeatable acquisition route. Those are hypotheses to investigate, not facts hidden inside a compelling founder story.
pages.body: A real business model needs verified context and relevant unit definitions. This document supplies no market size, revenue forecast, customer commitment or investment return.

pages.title: Show the roles the work requires.
pages.lead: The work would need product judgement, contextual inquiry and careful handling of source boundaries. We can describe those responsibilities without pretending that a complete team has been appointed. The next conversation should ask which capabilities are actually present and which need support.
pages.body: Replace role categories with named people only when their involvement and biographies are confirmed. This template contains no appointments, endorsements or staffing commitments.

pages.title: Connect resources to learning gates.
pages.lead: Our illustrative planning model allocates 100 teaching units: 45 to discovery, 35 to a prototype question and 20 to review. These are not currency, a real budget or an amount we are raising. The point is to connect each proposed resource category with a question that must be answered before a larger commitment.
pages.body: The model JSON/CSV preserves the 45+35+20=100 arithmetic. A real financing ask needs an actual entity, verified plan, terms and appropriate advice outside this fictional script.

pages.title: Close with an honest invitation.
pages.lead: If the problem and the proposed learning route seem worth investigating, the next step is a focused conversation about evidence, responsibilities and the right conditions for further work. We would rather leave you with one clear question than imply a level of progress we have not established.
pages.body: End on the specific response sought. This is not an offer of securities, a promise of funding or a request to act on invented terms. Preserve the fictional-source note in shared copies.
